audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer used two fabricated/misassigned ability names. spikes[0] called W 'The Pack dash' that 'closes the gap'; spikes[1] called R 'Call of the Pack' and described it as 'extra dashes, packmates, and healing'. Both are wrong slots.
audit.why: Riot's kit: W is The Call of the Pack — 400 range, 26/24/22/20/18s, makes her UNTARGETABLE and empowers the pack; it is not a dash. E is Eviscerate — the 450-range dash on 11/10/9/8/7s that heals her packmates. R is Hounds' Pursuit — a 900-range lock-on dash on 110/95/80s that recasts for a shield. The old text merged W and E into R.
audit.corrected: spikes[0] now names E Eviscerate as the 450 dash on 11s; spikes[1] now names R Hounds' Pursuit as the 900 lock-on dash that recasts for a shield; early and wants.foe[1] no longer call W a dash.
sources: enemyKit W/E/R text, ranges and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: diff read HARD at 8/10 while the matchup is 49.31% over 2951 games and the level chart itself hands Lux the last two stages. The full-layer phases[].side also read Naafiri on all seven rows while content win[] and the packet chart read Naafiri x4, Skill, Lux, Lux — the page rendered two different answers for levels 6, first item and 2+ items.
audit.why: Lux loses the first four levels to Darkin Daggers shove plus free packmate chip at 900, then flips it: Naafiri has to close 900 into a 1175 root and has no hard CC to stop Final Spark. That is an even lane with an early deficit, not an 8/10.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN, diffRating 6.5/10 (carry threat left at 8.5/10 — she is still a genuine assassin). phases[4..6].side moved to Skill/Lux/Lux with matching ratings and whys, aligning the full layer to the content layer and the packet.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0-3 had side=Naafiri but whys that described Lux dominating ('your chip engine', 'the root threat re-prices every step'). The row said one thing and the sentence under it said the opposite.
audit.why: At levels 1-3 Naafiri owns the lane: Darkin Daggers at 900 with packmate chip, then Eviscerate at 450 on an 11s cooldown out-trades a Q-E-auto.
audit.corrected: All four early whys rewritten to state Naafiri's advantage and what Lux does about it, matching the unchanged side values.

audit.why: Hounds' Pursuit is 110s at rank 1 and 80s at rank 3 — the single longest window in the lane and the one that decides when Lux may step up. Eviscerate is 11s to 7s; The Call of the Pack is 26s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with all three real cooldowns and the untargetability warning on W.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page said that Naafiri can go untargetable through a committed burst, or that Hounds' Pursuit's recast grants a shield.
audit.why: W and E both carry the untargetable flag and R carries both untargetable and shield in Riot's own text; missingInteractions flags all three for this exact matchup.
audit.corrected: tradeBad and breakdown.cooldowns now warn against spending R into The Call of the Pack; enemyWin and dontsFull[2].d now state the R recast shield. Anti-heal timing was already present in report[8].t and is kept.

audit.whatIsWrong: Eleven fields called Naafiri 'he/his/him', and two bullets were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles.
audit.why: Naafiri is female per champ-gender.js; the bullet bodies contradicted their own titles.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed; dosFull[1].d rewritten about wave position and flanks, dontsFull[2].d about greeding the detonation at half health.

notes: Chart: the full layer disagreed with the content layer AND the packet on rows 4, 5 and 6 (full said Naafiri on all seven; content and packet said Naafiri x4 / Skill / Lux / Lux). I moved the full layer to match, because content already holds the correct values — so there is no paired win[] edit to write for those three rows. This is the reverse of the usual failure mode: the fix REMOVES a cross-layer disagreement rather than creating one. If apply-proposals.js holds the chart group for want of a win[] twin, the correct manual action is to accept the three side/rating/why edits as-is; win[4]='Skill', win[5]='Lux', win[6]='Lux' are already on disk. Biggest content win here is the two fabricated ability descriptions: W was described as a gap-closing dash (it is a 400-range untargetable pack empower) and R was named 'Call of the Pack' with W's and E's effects. Left templated but ungroundable: breakdown.carry, breakdown.early and breakdown.mid are Lux-generic; report[3].t and report[13].t now duplicate the old tradeGood/tradeBad and ahead text and are out of sync, but the sweep caps report rewrites so I left them for a mechanical resync. Unverified and not written: whether Light Binding lands on Naafiri mid-Hounds'-Pursuit or is eaten by the dash's untargetability window — the kit flags R as untargetable, which would make 'root her mid-R' unreliable, but Riot's text does not say when that window opens or closes.
